title: Supply and inventory
purpose: When a best seller is about to run out, cash is stuck in stock, or a cost or delivery surprise lands, open Supply and inventory to know what to order, what to clear and what each order really costs to reach the door.
fires: the stock spreadsheet updated on Fridays, the founder's gut on order size, the forwarder's invoice as the first news of a cost change, and the carrier's monthly summary nobody reads.
not_for: a print-on-demand or dropship store that holds no stock and places no supplier orders.

jobs.job: When our best seller is on track to run out the week before Black Friday, tell me now, while there is still time to order, and how much to order, so I do not lose the biggest sales week of the year
jobs.circumstance: Early September, the hero product sells faster than planned, the factory needs 8 weeks plus 4 at sea, no one has done the math

progress.functional: know the stockout date for each top product against lead time, and the order size that covers the peak
progress.emotional: stop the sick feeling of watching the best week sell out on day 2
progress.social: tell the partner and the ad team the peak is covered, and look in control

jobs.hire_today: the founder's stock spreadsheet updated on Fridays, or an ops freelancer, or gut feel
jobs.fire: the Friday spreadsheet and the gut call on order size

forces.push: a stockout at peak loses the year's best sales and wastes the ads pointed at the product
forces.pull: a warning with the date and the units, while there is still time
forces.habit: we order the same amount as last time
forces.anxiety: what if I over-order and sit on stock in January

jobs.little_hire: every week, daily in the 12 weeks before peak

watch.metric: days of stock left against supplier lead time plus buffer, for the top 20 products by gross profit
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS) and supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

drives.metric: stockout days on the top 20 products in peak weeks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the hero sold out 5 days before Black Friday last year, about $60,000 lost. After: the reorder was placed 14 weeks out and stock lasted to mid December.
jobs.not_for: a print-on-demand or dropship store that holds no stock

jobs.job: When the bank balance is low and the warehouse is full, tell me how much cash sits in stock that has not sold in 6 months and how to turn it back into money, so I can pay for ads and the products that sell
jobs.circumstance: Month end, $40,000 in the bank, $300,000 of stock on the shelves, ad budget cut, the accountant asks what is not moving

progress.functional: know slow and dead stock by product, at landed cost, with a plan to clear each
progress.emotional: stop the knot in the stomach every time I look at the bank
progress.social: show a lender, partner or accountant a real plan

jobs.hire_today: the accountant's stock value at year end, or a clearance sale when things get desperate
jobs.fire: the year-end stock number and the panic sale

forces.push: cash stuck in stock cannot pay for ads or new products, and storage costs every month
forces.pull: the dead stock list with the cash each could free
forces.habit: we hope slow stock will sell eventually
forces.anxiety: what if a clearance cheapens the brand

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and whenever cash is tight

watch.metric: value of stock with no sale in 180 days, at landed cost, monthly
watch.source: Shopify inventory or the warehouse system (3PL or WMS) and landed cost in supplier and purchase order records in the brand brain

drives.metric: cash tied up in stock, in days of sales

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $90,000 of stock has not sold in 6 months. After: $35,000, with $40,000 back as cash through bundles and a quiet outlet sale.
jobs.not_for: a store that makes to order and holds no stock

watch.source: Shopify fulfilment events and the shipping app (ShipStation, AfterShip)
